# The last format-1 commits, which FS-72's T3 rollback builds real binaries from (EVS2-M10-30; §22.10's "a rollback to
# format-1 binaries", D-PHASE-10, FS-72). A setting cannot prove what old code does, so T3's rollback runs evs and
# taskworker built from these commits over data format 2 wrote. sidecar's and server's are each the parent of the first
# commit of EVS2-M10-05, which first let an engine take a format-2 value. EVS2-M2-01's reservations and its 503 for a
# push to a format-2 repo/ are in both, but not its guard for format-2 data (evsservice/format1_guard.go: no fold,
# page-out, path-epoch copy or marker collection on a format-2 repo), which landed in one commit with EVS2-M10-05's
# raise, so no commit is a format-1 binary carrying it: which build a rollback goes to is question
# evs2-m10-30-format1-rollback-binary, and these pins stand until it is answered.
#
# sidecar: the module evs's engine and taskworker's evs jobs link
# server:  evshost and taskworker, which host them
# the rest: the siblings server's go.mod replaces (../<repo>), each at its sidecar branch's first-parent commit before
#           sidecar's pin was committed (2026-11-10T02:21:04-06:00), all on go 1.27.3's line, before QD-674 moved every
#           go.mod to 1.27.4: a tree of these ten, each `git archive` of its commit into one directory, builds
#           server's ./cli/evs and ./cli/taskworker with go1.27.4, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly and
#           GOPROXY=off from the run's module cache (checked 2026-11-15)
